claims.claim: Reviewers describe the new player onboarding as confusing, noting that early missions lack clear instructions or explanations for objectives.

citations.review_text: super boring no idea what i have to do and the missions are to easy
The core gameplay is good but 90% of the games main appeal (warframes) are locked behind 40-60 hours or a weird trading system with no developer backing.

The new player experience can be extremely confusing, but unlike other online communities, people will run the early game stuff with you because they are also rewarded with materials and items.
A lot of high concept scifi plot elements, time traveling, world cultural themes from all different eras.

A lot of batsh-t insane plot elements keep the story, themes and aesthetics fresh.
There is NO other game like Warframe. Seriously. Let it sink its teeth into you. There will be numerous things to enjoy.

Don't even try to explain things about the game because there are surprises within that are worth discovering on your own. 

Also this game runs incredibly on low spec machines. Even intel iris can handle it.

This game is an absolute blast. That is, when it works. The movement and combat are incredibly fluid and rewarding, and I plan on keeping with it.

However, player beware: the onboarding and user experience are genuinely terrible. The game throws you into frantic, high-stakes missions with zero explanation of what you're supposed to do. You will fail—not because you lack skill or gear, but because the game itself refuses to communicate basic objectives.

Case in point: an early quest on Venus forces you to defend a drill, but never tells you to hunt down specific glowing enemies, grab their batteries, and manually feed the machine. To the pedantic out there, oh sure, it "tells" you in little tiny text off to the far left of your screen, which you won't notice as you're feverishly trying to fend off enemies. You're just left to get overwhelmed and fail the mission multiple times while fighting a broken onboarding system.

Expect to keep a wiki open on a second monitor just to understand what you're supposed to do. The core loop is worth it, but the developers desperately need to fix their UX. Play it, but keep Google handy.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight fast-paced movement, fluid combat mechanics, and cooperative gameplay as positive aspects.

citations.review_text: really fun game that scratches the looter shooter itch that has been left in the wake of the death of other unnamed games cough cough. the community is very welcoming and really happy to help people learn the game and all it has to offer. I also love the movement in this game.

I've known of this game for a long time but never played it until now. I can say so far it's a pretty nice Co-Op PVE or just to play solo. I haven't seen that much of a team work requirement to the Co-Op aspect, people kinda just go their own way and slash through enemies. That being said the combat is very fluid, once you learn the game's controls it becomes very fun. Very fantasy space like, the story is fun as well.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Warframe is easily one of the best free-to-play games on Steam. The amount of content is staggering, with countless missions, Warframes, weapons, and quests that can keep you entertained for hundreds or even thousands of hours.

The fast-paced movement and fluid combat make every mission enjoyable, and the progression system always gives you something new to chase. The developers continue to support the game with regular updates, new story content, and meaningful improvements, showing a real passion for the community.

While the game can feel overwhelming at first because of its depth, sticking with it is well worth the effort. Whether you enjoy co-op gameplay, collecting gear, or diving into an ever-expanding sci-fi universe, Warframe has something for everyone.

An outstanding game that keeps getting better with age. Highly recommended.

- Moth

I’ve been playing this game since 2014, and it remains one of my favorites. It’s accessible for both veteran gamers and newcomers; a friend started just a week ago and has already reached MR 13. For a free title, the depth and breadth of content are remarkable.

The community is another standout. New players can easily find support by hopping into a session or using the in-game community tools—there are many experienced players willing to help. I’ve met great people and made lasting memories.

The developers clearly care about the player base, which shows in ongoing updates and engagement. The story is genuinely cinematic—there are moments of high excitement and others that are unexpectedly moving.

If I had to rate it, this would be my number one game. The creativity, cooperative play, and overall enjoyment make it an experience not to miss, especially with friends.


P.s. Can't wait for you to play Tenno

P.s.s. Wish me a happy birthday if you made it this far.

citations.review_text:
Used to love this game, but cannot recommend it anymore
[NOTE FOR READERS]: I am writing this on a new Steam account (hence the low hours tracked here). I am a long-time veteran player who has put hundreds of hours into this game on my previous main account.

1. Customer Support & Account Security Risk
Automated flag systems and rigid customer support make long-time accounts feel entirely unsafe. Getting hit with suspensions or bans without a transparent human review or a functional appeal process completely invalidates hundreds of hours of progression. Investing time or money into a profile that can be arbitrarily bricked by support is a massive risk which sucks.

2. Artificial Time-Gates & Slot Monetization
Starting over exposes the underlying core loop: excessive time-gating designed to push Platinum sales. Foundry crafting timers (24 to 72 hours per item/frame), hard daily Standing caps, and strictly capped initial Warfrme/Weapon inventory slots turn progression into a slog. If you aren't constantly trading on third-party sites to fund slots, your gameplay variety is locked down hard.

3. Floaty, Low-Interaction Combat Engine
From an action-game perspective, the combat system lacks physical feedback. Physics interactions, hit-stop frames, stamina management, and enemy telegraphing are nonexistent. Movement relies on high-velocity bullet-jump animation loops through repetitive corridor tilesets, while combat devolves into spamming screen-wide AoE ability scripts to wipe room-scale horde AI. It lacks the mechanical weight and satisfaction of dedicated action RPGs.

5. Non-Existent In-Game Community
In-game chat channels are functionally unusable for social interaction. Region and Trade channels are dominated by hyper-fast scrolling macro spammers, trade-bot filters (WTB / WTS), and automated text blocks. Actual community engagement has completely migrated off-platform to Discord or third-party web markets, leaving the in-game UI feeling like an exchange floor rath…

One of the Best Free-to-Play Games Ever Made

Warframe is easily one of the best free-to-play games I've ever played. The movement is incredibly smooth, the combat is fast-paced and satisfying, and there are so many unique Warframes and weapons to unlock that it never gets boring.

What impressed me the most is that you can earn almost everything through gameplay without being forced to spend money. The developers continue to release major updates, new story content, and quality-of-life improvements, making the game feel fresh even after hundreds of hours.

The learning curve can be overwhelming at first because there's so much content, but once you understand the systems, it's hard to stop playing. The community is also very helpful to new players.

If you enjoy looter shooters, sci-fi, character customization, or grind-based progression with rewarding gameplay, Warframe is absolutely worth trying.

Highly recommended!

Amazing graphics and nice fluid movement/combat system. For it being a free game, there's a ton of content and the only downfall to any of it is the grind. However, you don't need to grind too much for the low/mid grade stuff, and the grinding is actually enjoyable most the time. Just be aware that you're gonna be sinking a lot of hours to accomplish anything.

Very muchly doggy doo doo.

I remember being a tender youthful lad of 17 first playing this in the early 2010s and experiencing such heights of joy as I ran around the maps slicing Grineer soldiers and using the same ground pound move over and over and upgrading my skills. But vigour was quickly soured once the first 5 starter levels were completed and I then had to spend hours punching through masses of sh1ttily fully-shielded eraser-blockheaded soldiers and metal emus who could stun lock you. 

More and more expansions were released but nothing was explained as to how one would realistically progress beyond the metal emus other than, "spend more of your parents money to get to the better stuff". They released doggos, fairy wings, SPACE, and other expansions into the game. Disheartened, witnessing flashbacks from my World of Warcraft and City of Heroes days I realized that perhaps I would never get to experience these joys whilst under my strict parents thumb.

Then, years later, I rejoined, partly because of some sick cover I saw of Queen that someone had recorded in-game and uploaded onto the Youtubes. I started up the game again, eager to witness what fresh new joys awaited me almost a decade later.....and I was still stuck fighting emus and block heads. Not long after I had the benefit of witnessing a team mate flying through the map armed with a little laser pistol, instantly killing any enemy he looked at.

At that point I realized that, maybe, now that I had my own funds and mine own personal credit card, I too could perhaps enjoy maybe a sliver of enjoyment that these other veterans had seemed to so experience (after generous donations into the developers bank accounts). Perhaps I too could walk through the levels clicking and dragging my mouse across the enemies without having to activate any of my grey matter. Then I laughed and continued on with life.

Spend literal days waiting on weapons and warframes to finish building (That's always been a thing but as a new player now with the metric F**Kton of things in the game now to build. GOOD LUCK) 
There are better games to waste your life away with. I wouldn't say this one left me with any satisfaction or rewarding feelings in the …

-Got convinced on playing this game 
-Confused as heck on what to do so I went to google and so I went and search warframe fashion
-Saw a cool looking rhino fashion frame
-Grinded till I got rhino
-Fashioned him and ts goes hard 

It is a very "Hell Yeah" type of grindy game and i'm loving it all so far ❤
Too much grind for a game but whos put 56 hours in a game where you sit down playing and grind for hours and complain about it . SMH
Very grindy and the missions were all pretty similar. A lot of my time in the game just felt like doing the same mission over and over with different texture packs.
Lot of grinding but it is free, is fun, and the story gets really good the deeper you go.
A great power fantasy game with a good story and great devs. Parts of the game can feel grindy, but I am a fan of being able to earn my way though the game.

If you like the idea of a space ninja game with flexibility, lore, grinding, and community, Warframe is for you. claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has a steep learning curve and explains very little to new players, requiring them to rely heavily on external search engines, wikis, or other players for guidance.

citations.review_text:
This game is honestly? Pretty good, especially for a free to play game. It has a very varied game-play loop, plenty of things to do.

I'm abit torn between giving it a negative rating or a positive one I'll admit..

I've never played a game where I had to google and use other search engines to find answers as much as this, ultimately it's what got me away from it aswell in frustration, it's infuriating how little is actually explained about events, what you unlock through the missions ( Zones like Duviri, Zariman etc. ) etc ( Such as Kuva liches for examble. )
Definetly NOT for new players.
Not just that, but the story as interesting as it honestly is, jumps from quest to quest. You reach a point where you unlock Duviri for examble and you just jump into it because, why not? You've done that with the rest. Unknown to you, you get a massive spoiler by just the start. But then again, it's a free-to-play game, so maybe that's on me.
Generally though I feel like quite a few MMO based games today has a problem with attracting new players because of over-bloated systems, lying forgotten instead of streamlining them into the newer ones.

The Combat is Insane: It's the exact opposite of holding tight, tactical angles in CSGO. Instead, you are literally bullet-jumping across the map, gliding through the air, and slicing up hordes of bad guys like an absolute blender. The combat flow is pure, chaotic fun and makes you feel completely untouchable.

Zero Explanation: the game explains absolutely nothing. You get dropped in, and suddenly you're staring at fifty different menus, random resources, and weird space jargon. You pretty much have to keep the wiki open on a second monitor just to figure out what the heck you are actually supposed to be doing.

The Endless Grind: The grind here is incredibly real. It makes the hardcore endgame loot chase in Diablo look pretty straightforward. You'll find yourself farming the exact same boss thirty times just to get one specific blueprint drop. And when you finally get the parts? The game makes you wait real-world days for the crafting to finish.
Probably the best free game, tons of contents, a great community, and very fun gameplay. However it is quite complicated at first and you will need external help to understand some things.

Came back after about 6 years, back then every waking hour was consumed by playing this freaking game. Now I decided to check back, and sure enough I feel its hooks sinking right back in.

The game is pretty fun and will provide you with a lot of memorable moments if you're patient enough, but I really should warn any potential new players that, after some time, you should eventually look up guides or go into the wiki to look up anything you don't understand. WF is notorious for not explaining a lot of important things to this day, and it's not intuitive enough to quickly learn on your own, but this also means a lot of experienced players understand this and will help newer players when possible.

Also I'm not joking about how this game consumes your life, there is so much to do, and it's very easy to become sidetracked and spend many hours doing a lot other things if you don't get your priorities set up, which makes it doubly important to learn how the game works and what you should work towards if you wanna advance through all the content and not burn out.

So just pace yourself, and have fun.

claims.claim: Players can earn premium currency entirely for free through an in-game player trading system.

citations.review_text: It's free to play, you can trade in-game currency to buy the things you want, and it's fully developed, something a ton of games are lacking these days. I'm hooked. Really great game if you don't mind grinding for the things you want to obtain in it without spending in-real-life money.

i love this game a bit too much (look at my hours played XD) 
anywho this is a F2P game and the devs arnt cheep or greedy! trading items in game with other players lets you get platinum without paying a cent and still get special stuff or cosmetics, no ads ether, many characters and weapons of shooty and melee variety from bomb frizbees to lasers, explosions, snipers, bows, swords, hammers, guns ect, very scifi fantasy with stuff, good few sections of the game function like a whole other games at times (i see it as a good thing) divuri having rouglite elements and being darksouls-est, and railjack being nearly full space ship combat, theres variety even outside the normal games mission types, despite this game comeing out in like 2013 or something ago they still do new stuff to this day and over time updating older stuffs too, also music and character customization potential is nuts, everyone says fasion is the real end game XD and their not wrong.

also the "nightwave" is a battle pass like thing but 100% free, no p2w nothing on it, just play the game and do the lil missions it gives daily or weekly and you get REALLY nice free goodies

this game can be grindy at times and you gotta wait 12-24hours for most crafting stuff but hey your not forced to play 24-7 so your fine to take breaks or check in another day if your a cassual player :D and some warframes boost loot drops, but to keep that tangent short just look up what your after and look at many results or go to the official wiki

also this game is rated M for good reason, enemies have blood (i turned it off tho) and some skins for characters are pretty suggestive, (HOT WOMAN) and story and some lore you can dig into is bit dark when you really look into parts, main story wise game gives you fare warning, character skin wise you can just not use the skin, other players can but you can play solo mode (relays and hubs are always public tho)

also please turn off the global chat tab (in settings) you dont need that…

At first I thought it was a pay to win game, but things are earnable in-game, and even the premium currency can be obtained the same way through trading. When opening relics you can also click on which one of the ones the other players in your team unlocked and can have that one instead without the original player losing it, as if truly, as Lotus says, sharing in the bounty.
I am being currently stalked by Harrow, so I may actually stick around and get him in the end. At the time of writing, I quite recommend the game and quite like it.

THAT said, I am worried for what I saw of with fee fees and the story and all the rest, but so far I just find peace if fighting through hordes and traveling planets
I am orphaned and chased out from Destiny after they killed Io, Warframe is being a new place I am finding myself increasingly growing to like as somewhere I can stay

Warframe is the best F2P game you can find and I'm not exaggerating. It's a huge-grind kind of a game but you can earn anything by yourself, only if you want to. You can even earn premium currency for free in-game but you need to trade stuff with other players (are we in heaven yet?).

PLOT:
When it comes to the plot of the game, then let's just say it's divided into Old War (older content, and I'd say story with an ending) and New War (newer content, that is still not fully completed). 

GAMEPLAY:
Gameplay loop looks like this: we go into a mission -> we get resources -> we craft new stuff (characters, weapons, companions, pets, transformers etc.) -> we get stronger -> now repeat.

If you want to get something specific, character for example: you go into Arsenal -> choose warframe -> double click your specific frame -> when you hover your mouse over the "buy blueprint" button, you can read how to get the main blueprint (if its not buyable) and how to get the parts.

If something is unclear (which definetly a lot of things will be) you can ask people on chat (I recommend playing on english servers because there's a lot of people) OR you can use warframe wiki website.

The movement is awesome but you need to practice at the beginning. For PC (!) best movement combo is:
Ctrl + Space for the bullet jump -> Space for the double jump -> 2x Shift for the roll -> now repeat (you can also add holding RMB after double jump, to aim and fly in the air for a while, and then roll). Some characters also have movement abilities.

GRAPHICS:
Game looks cool on high and low settings (honestly im good at low settings and big fov) so you just need to run the game. This game also had a lot of upgrades in the context of graphics since the beginning (it's out for a long time now).

CONS:
My 2 main cons of the game are:
1. How long it takes to craft things - yeah I get it that it's a grindy game, but c'mon it's like 4 days (fastest possible) to craft a character, and it takes around 7-14 d…

1200+ hours in and there still soo much to do what a thrill.

Why do you play Warframe?
1. I was a huge Destiny player, some of my most fond teen memories while gaming so I followed them to Destiny 2 and time and time again they let me down, I kept with it since it was the only game of it's kind that I enjoyed playing. I tried hard to stay playing but when they made the light level cap they lost me for good, they made grinding mandatory instead of a choice for PVP. So it was a weekend evening and I saw a friend playing WARFRAME and it looked so good. So I tried it out and never looked back. It was everything I wanted + MORE.
2. I love the face that I can take a year break and even though there's so much new content I can still use my old build to continue playing. I never have to worry about oh I will need to grind so much just to be able to barely hang in and contribute in mission.
3. I love that if I really want to most things can be purchased with in-game currency PLAT that can be acquired by selling items in game. No need to purchase items with real money, for most things.
4.I love the huge discounts that 75% off plat discount I always buy because Warframe has got a customer for life.
5.The developers genuinely seem to enjoy building their game and so I know it's not money grab looking for a whale, but a team that listens to their consumers and their feedback and pivots based on that. Truly makes me feel like this game ain't going nowhere but UP.
6. The game is SOOO MASSIVE soo much to do it's never ending. There's always something to do and the best part is you're not forced to play activities. I have 1200 hours and have barely touched railjack, simply because I don't want to.
7. I've gone to one of their yearly Events called TENNOCON and it was so much fun, you could tell at a glance that the team behind Warframe is in it for the long haul not just for a corporate ladder climb.
8. The community, most people are nice and willing to help you out, there…

claims.claim: Crafting items, weapons, or warframes requires gathering resources and waiting real-world hours or days for completion, though timers can be bypassed with premium currency.

citations.review_text:
The Combat is Insane: It's the exact opposite of holding tight, tactical angles in CSGO. Instead, you are literally bullet-jumping across the map, gliding through the air, and slicing up hordes of bad guys like an absolute blender. The combat flow is pure, chaotic fun and makes you feel completely untouchable.

Zero Explanation: the game explains absolutely nothing. You get dropped in, and suddenly you're staring at fifty different menus, random resources, and weird space jargon. You pretty much have to keep the wiki open on a second monitor just to figure out what the heck you are actually supposed to be doing.

The Endless Grind: The grind here is incredibly real. It makes the hardcore endgame loot chase in Diablo look pretty straightforward. You'll find yourself farming the exact same boss thirty times just to get one specific blueprint drop. And when you finally get the parts? i have 292 hours in this chud of a game. do you know how much i can remember of the time i spent playing? not much. a solid 85% of time spent playing this game has been grinding the same stupid missions to get some slight, ultimately insignificant, progress. 

this is easily one of the worst, least rewarding, repetitive games ive ever played. if you have the time required to dump hundreds of hours just to get some weird cosmetics or, better yet, drag yourself through the sewage pit that is this game in general, gooning or drugs might be a healthier hobby.

HERES THE KICKER THOUGH!! i would UNIRONICALLY buy this game at full price of modern day AAA videogames if they just removed all the daily limits, the insignificant little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tasks required to progress, lowered the time to craft items/weapons/frames, and stopped putting limits on inventory space. there is ZERO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason i should have to spend my time clocking in every day to do 3 missions for a civilization, then have to STOP playing because i cant progress anymore.

this game has so much potential to actually be decent, but instead they have decided it is more profitable to be a FTP, daily grind, annoying game

i first started playing this game on xbox, if it weren't for the ability to get my data from xbox i probably wouldn't have picked this back up. the wait time to get things done screams prehistoric mobile game greed. this system is way out dated and should b retired. i hate it, but it is a free game. that being said i do enjoy for the most part the rest of the game. people will tell u it takes a long time to get into this, and it will, mainly due to having to wait to finish building things (typically 3 1/2 days real time for warframes) but first you have to collect whatever material and blueprints that are necessary to build it. it can b grindy depending on what ur after... but if u are able to push past that, and some of the story that it makes you do to unlock the rest of the game, u will enjoy it. it really is one of those that u have to devote a good portion of time to enjoy. i will say this isn't for everyone it wont b everyone's cup of tea...

6.75 / 10

A mixed positive review, the gameplay can be very fun (though a bit opaque sometimes) but you can feel the microtransactions and the systems are put in place to drive you towards them.

Even if you grind to unlock a nice weapon, frame, or anything else the crafting times for the finish product are ~3 days for anything notable. You can of course buy the premium currency (platinum) to speed it up.
There are trading options, but the in-game trade system is limited and only lets you make a certain number of trades a day, making it hard to rapidly rack up platinum even if you have the items to do so. You can of course increase the number of trades you may make, but this requires leveling that is a long term goal rather than any short term possibility. 

Outside of the complaints about the microtransaction-based systems, I find the fluid movement and gameplay fun, and of course it helps to hop on with a friend. Pubbing is a good experience, and it feels interesting when you become the guy killing everyone on the map before anyone can catch up that you saw when you were level 1.

People have sunk thousands of hours into this game on a single account, and I would be lying if I said there wasn't something to it that could keep you hooked that long.

imagine playing destiny, except every time you get a gun you need to grind resources and then wait 72 hours for it to craft before youre allowed to use it. but thats fine! since you can use premium currency to craft it instantly
if you look up the community's opinion about this, they think it's totally fine because you should be "taking a break" or "doing other things in the game" while waiting for the timer.

imagine wanting a specific build-enabling mod for your weapon or warframe. spend 20min doing a node for a 5% chance at getting it to drop
but thats fine because you can buy a mod bundle containing the mod you want for premium currency.
you can earn this premium currency ingame by opening lootboxes over and over for hours, hoping eventually you get a full blueprint set of a prime that you can sell for $5 worth of platinum

the game shamelessly tries to nickle and dime you wherever it can.
somehow, the community have deluded themselves into thinking this is "not p2w" and is "the most generous f2p monetisation system". i dont think the warframe community have played other video games
the entire game is a collection of dark patterns. gacha studios wish they had this much of a cultish fanbase

all of this wouldnt even be that horrible if frame&weapon slots didnt exist. there are 65 non-prime warframes. if you want to own more than 3, the game demands money. imagine if genshin impact had a separate microtransaction for "character slots". what are we doing here?
